Ben / Dylan — hi, David from Privacy & Ops. Quick technical rundown and what we can produce as evidence.

1) No-training / model improvement
- We can contractually commit (DPA addendum) that customer content will not be used to train or evaluate Redwood models. Operationally we map customer tenancy to isolated serving pools and maintain a policy that prevents ingestion of customer content into our training pipelines.
- Evidence: addendum text + an ops attestation describing the gating points. We also provide a short internal runbook extract showing the ingestion gating.

2) Subprocessors and residency
- Attached: redwood_subprocessors_20261011.csv (column: name, role, region, SOC/Security cert). We will mark which subprocessors process EU tenant workloads.
- For EU tenant requests we support region-locked serving in eu-central-1 and an onshore KMS option via our marketplace KMS partners.

3) KMS & keys
- We use customer-managed keys (CKMs) or our managed onshore KMS partners. If you opt for CKM, keys never leave the region. We can provide KMS attestation and a hash of key rotation events for audit.

4) Data handling & outputs
- Ephemeral KV caching is configurable per-tenant. For Orchard we propose: ephemeral KV disabled by default, prefix caching only allowed with explicit consent, and a retention window of 0 days for conversational logs unless otherwise agreed.
- Outputs: standard approach is outputs are licensed to the tenant. We will include explicit derivative IP language ("Tenant retains rights to tenant-generated outputs; Redwood retains rights to model parameters and non-tenant-specific improvements").

Attachments: redwood_subprocessors_20261011.csv, SOC2_Type2_2025.pdf (redacted), sample_runbook_excerpt.txt (ops extract).

If Orchard requires stricter controls (complete on-prem or air-gapped private deployment), we can discuss Redwood Private — we can scope in a separate conversation.

I’ll draft proposed addendum language and share a DocuSign link. If you prefer to see track-changes on your redlines, we can do that too.

-David
David Kim
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

David / Dylan — thanks for the fast and useful reply. A few clarifications from legal/procurement:

- Our ask on "no training" needs to include: (a) prohibition on using customer-provided content for model training or evaluation; (b) prohibition on using de-identified or anonymized derivatives for training unless we explicitly opt in.
- We need the DPA addendum to state that derivative outputs produced by Redwood models as a result of tenant requests are licensed to Orchard under exclusive-use terms for Orchard's internal product features (we can share sample wording).
- Residency: EU-only processing for EU tenant traffic (both memory/KV and token processing) unless explicitly routed by us. At-rest can be in EU but we need guarantees on cross-border transfers.

Procurement would like to get this signed by EOM if possible. Please send the addendum + DocuSign and note any items that require engineering time (e.g., CKM enablement, regional KMS setup).

-Ben
